## {#today .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.todaymeta}
A one-day workshop in four parts, on the housing-audit case
:::

:::: {.todaybox}
::: {.nonincremental .fs-85}
1. The claim and credibility – science and its crisis, the three Rs, SCORE and Multi100, and the paper
2. The estimand and the causal graph – five analysts, estimands, and the graph of the experiment
3. The reproduction – one of the five reanalyses reproduced from the public file
4. Robustness – the menu, the class chart, the curve, the new audit and one preregistered analysis
:::
::::

::: {.todaytake .fs-85}
You leave with a reproduced result, an estimand statement and a causal graph of your own, a preregistered analysis, and your results on a live class multiverse
:::

::: {.todaymeta}
Work along in the browser lab, solo or in pairs, or in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) if you have installed the workspace
:::

::: notes
Welcome – good to have you here. A full day, in four parts. The first sets up everything else: what we are doing when we do social science, why people say it is in crisis, the three very large studies that measured the problem, and the published experiment that we work on all day, in which a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing. The second asks what question the claim of that paper actually answers. In the third you reproduce one of the five independent reanalyses of the claim, whichever you choose. The fourth is the centre of the day: you vary the analysis yourself, we read the chart that the class builds against every justifiable analysis, we meet the new study that tested the claim again, and you settle on the one analysis that you would publish.
:::
